caba60ee-e48f-11f1-899a-9375cafeb724.one_liner: A macro-trading podcast argues the Fed is tightening into a slowdown it's only now recognizing, with AI-driven credit market stress (unsecured debt shut to data centers) and bond yields stuck despite weakening growth data.
caba60ee-e48f-11f1-899a-9375cafeb724.recap: Hosts on Forward Guidance discuss the Anthropic IPO (pricing at ~$2 trillion, aggressive unlock schedule, heavy retail demand) as emblematic of AI-trade exhaustion: token prices are collapsing even as usage rises, squeezing frontier-model margins. They tie this to Nvidia's ~40% drawdown and note credit markets have effectively closed to data center/neocloud financing, forcing reliance on equity raises instead of unsecured debt — a reversal of the 'circular financing' dynamic that propped up hyperscaler capex. On rates, they argue the Fed is behind the curve: FOMC minutes this week flagged AI-driven inflation risk just as the AI build-out is visibly slowing, and hawkish rhetoric from regional Fed presidents (Waller floating 50bp hike odds) is keeping bonds from rallying even as equal-weight equities, housing starts, and commodities (oil down 35%, copper weak per Druckenmiller) all signal a broadening slowdown. They note real rates are near GFC-era highs after the Fed reversed heavy repo/liquidity operations ($40bn/month) earlier in the year. Comparisons are drawn to 2018 (weak labor market, policy mistake risk) versus 2022 (inflation overshoot), concluding current conditions combine the worst of both. Treasury's Bessent is notably absent after a year of active market intervention. They argue a slow, controlled 'bleed' rather than a V-shaped crash is needed to actually durably lower inflation, and expect gold/Bitcoin and duration trades to wait until slowdown confirmation.
